title: Standard forms and adhesion: editorial notes and questions
summary: Read the surrounding notes and questions alongside the principal cases. The complete assigned pages are preserved here.
notes:
Carnival Cruise Lines, Inc. v. Shute: Carnival links assent, adhesion, remedies, and Civil Procedure. Keep the majority’s conceded-notice premise separate from the disputed notice questions in Specht, Hill, Klocek, and Anderson.

Graham v. Scissor-Tail, Inc.: Graham prevents two oversimplifications: sophistication does not establish bargaining freedom, and knowledge of a term does not establish its substantive enforceability.

Doe v. Great Expectations: This case shows how legislation can impose terms and remedies that the printed agreement omits. It connects informed contracting, mandatory consumer protection, and recovery of payments.
